$comment: Tools and what they cut (docs/adr/0067-stone-axe-and-chopping.md). A tool is an item (shared/inventory/inventory.json names it) with a `kind` from a fixed vocabulary (`axe`: chops the `woods`). A swing cuts `biteM` into open wood when its plane crosses the grain; its share is `along + (across - along) * |cos θ|^sharpness`, θ the angle between the swing plane's normal and the grain. Wood cut deeper than a side's open notch binds: a swing into a kerf cuts `bite / (1 + kerf / bindM)`. A chunk comes out when both bands of a side are cut past its notch; a swing aimed at the band cut deeper lands in the other (the open wood), so one aim notches (BUGS.md #75). `woods`: the blocks an axe cuts (by name; their grain is their `axis` property), when a standing one falls (`fellFraction` of its cross-section cut) and a lying one is cut through (`buckFraction`), what a cut-through length drops (`buckDrops`, as a block's `drops`) and the chips a swing knocks out (`chips`: how many, their colour, speed m/s and size m; the client's particles). A tool's `held` is the item of shared/characters/characters.json a hand shows holding it for a level swing, `heldVertical` for a vertical one (two holds). A tool's `swing` is its feel and its path (the owner, 2026-11-08: weighty first-person melee): `windupS` before the arc, `activeS` the arc's sweep (the head travels `arcDeg` at `reachM` from the eye in `samples` steps, screen right to left for a level swing, top to bottom for a vertical one; the first solid cell on the path is hit, the server sweeping the same arc), `hitStopS` the pause on impact, `recoverHitS` after a hit and `recoverMissS` after a miss (a looser follow-through), `camera` the view's sway with the swing per swing kind (`level`, `vertical`; owner, 2026-11-12: "The camera could have some sway with the chop"; docs/CHARACTERS.md §5.2): `keys` over the phase time `t` (0 the swing's start, 1 the wind-up's end, 2 the arc's end, 3 a miss's recovery's end; at rest at 0 and 3), each `yaw` degrees toward the screen's right, `pitch` up, `roll` the view leaning right and `bob` [right, up, back] metres, eased between keys; `kick` the jolt at contact (the same offsets, dying over `decayS`; a miss kicks at `miss` of it as the head passes the arc's middle, a hit into a wood at 1, a bounce at `bounce`); the view only (never the aim), off with Settings → Motion → Camera sway, `staminaCost` what a swing will draw when stamina exists (unused until then), `swish` and `bounce` its sound events (shared/sounds; a bounce: not a wood), `rustle` the event of a swing that cleared blocks and `rustleLeaves` the leaves each cleared cell scatters (the client's particles). A tool's `clears` are the blocks (by name; not woods) its swing goes through and breaks on the way (owner, 2026-11-09: the axe clears leaves): every one the arc touches is broken (dropping its block's `drops` where blocks are not unlimited), and the head goes on to the wood behind (chopped) or another solid (a bounce). A wood's `fellWedge` is chopped as that wood, never cleared (WORK_QUEUE item 26; owner, 2026-11-12: the stump keeps its gash): a hit bites it and wears the tool, and it comes down cut through like the standing log (its `fellFraction`), dropping the wood's `buckDrops`; a tool's `clears` naming one fails. A wood's `leaves` are shaken down from that leaf block within `radiusM` and `heightM` above the hit on each hit, its `sway` leans the standing tree from `fromFraction` of the cross-section cut up to `maxDeg` at the fell fraction, and its `sounds` are each hit's sound event by the cut's fraction (`from` rising from 0). A wood's `cut` is how its cuts are carved into the cell's mesh (the client's; ADR 0067 §11): `tile` the atlas tile of the fresh-wood faces inside (shared/textures/materials.json's `tiles`; none: the block's end-grain tile) and `tint` a colour multiplying it (warm, so the wood stays tan in shade under the sky's and the ground's light), `open` the notch's opening along the grain per metre of its depth (its V), `kerfWidthM` the kerf slits' width (a cut without bites: an older save's or server's), `bite` each hit's bite (WORK_QUEUE item 26; owner, 2026-11-12: the slice "should align more with the dirt and stone ones"): a V the axe head's size where it struck, `widthM` its mouth across the side, its two ends sloping in over `endsM`, a hit on a spot already bitten (in that band) landing `step` × the width beside it so the bites widen and join into the notch; the notch grows by the bite rule (WORK_QUEUE item 18; owner, 2026-11-12: "Yes the notch should grow to follow the 50% rule"): after k of the swings to fell it has carved k × ½ × the log's volume ÷ those swings, one V `x` m deep, its mouth along the grain `bandM` at least and `x / depthPerMouth` past it (the cell's length at most), each bite widened to `x × widthPerDepth` across the side (the head's width at least), `cracks` the crack overlay round the bites (a set of shared/textures/cracks.json, `stages` by the share of the fell or buck fraction cut, `strength`; BLOCK_DAMAGE.md §6.3). A wood's `fellWedge` (a stored-ramp block, a carrier) is what felling leaves (Phase 55 T2; owner, 2026-11-09): the cut cell split along its diagonal, the stump keeping its upright ramp rising away from the notch and the trunk's new bottom its upside-down ramp; none: the cut cell goes; `fellWedgeTrunk` how the trunk's ramp lies (`matching`, the default: parallel to the stump's; `open`: the notch's upper face, thin at the notch, the two ramps a V gash open toward the side chopped; the log's, owner 2026-11-12: "2 half blocks one upside down one right side up, both with the 'short side' facing the cut"); `fellTip` the trunk's tip toward the notch as a share of `felling`'s topple spin (owner, 2026-11-09: "make the tree tip if needed, like we used to, maybe 3/4 of the force"; 0.75 left a short trunk standing on the matching wedge, so the log's is 1; 0: none). A block's `breakWith` (shared/blocks) names the tool kind breaking it needs where blocks are not unlimited (adventure: logs need an axe). A `weapon` (WORK_QUEUE item 35; owner, 2026-11-12: "bring in the swords ... as weapons"): a tool of kind `weapon` cuts no wood (no `biteM`, `bindM`, `across`, `along`, `sharpness`, `clears`, `chop2`); its `swing` is swept as the axe's, and at contact the server hurts the creatures the arc crosses (a player's swing: animals and NPCs, never a player; shared/creatures `health`, `hitRadiusM`, `drops`), the head stopping at the first solid block: `weapon.damage` the health one hit takes, `knockbackM` how far it pushes the creature away from the striker along the ground, `knockbackMps` and `liftMps` the push (m/s, away along the ground and up) a connecting hit gives a player (WORK_QUEUE item 38; owner, 2026-11-12: "Villagers should be able to hurt players.": an NPC's strike, the player taking `damage` as health, cause `Weapon`; players never strike players), `maxTargets` the most creatures one swing hits (in the order the arc meets them), `durability` the hits it survives (worn once per creature hit, as `durability.items`; none: it never wears); `guard` its swordplay (owner, 2026-11-12: "if you hit enemy sword within an angle threshold of perpendicular you're blocked, if within an angle of parallel it connects"): `stances` each stance's blade roll in the holder's view (`level` 0, `vertical` 90; a strike's blade is its swing kind's; `blade` the raised blade as others see it, its `grip` and `tip` in metres from the holder's feet [right, up, ahead], fitted to the third-person `raisedPose` (a clip_probe test keeps them within 0.1 m): a clash's sparks fly where the swing's arc meets it, BUGS.md #86), a strike on a defender's raised blade (its stance, facing the striker within `frontDeg`) within `blockWithinDeg` of perpendicular is blocked (no damage, a clash; the striker recoils for `recoilS`), within `connectWithinDeg` of parallel connects, between them glances (`glanceDamage` of the damage); attacking drops the defender's block for its swing. Defenders are creatures or NPCs holding a sword, and players with a raised block against an NPC's strike. Prototype content (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1). Run `node shared/tools/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails if the generated files are stale.

weapon.level: Sword: level stance (tap right click: vertical, hold: block)
weapon.vertical: Sword: vertical stance (tap right click: level, hold: block)

chop2.$comment: The chopping prototype (docs/WORK_QUEUE.md item 7, ADR 0067 amendment; owner 2026-11-11), behind a switch until approved: `enabled` its default (false: today's chopping; dev `?chop=v2` turns it on for a local world). Each chop at the crosshair removes a tool's `chop2.bite` of the cross-section on the side hit (along the grain: the wood's `chop2.along` of that); the first side cut is the notch (a V), a cut on another side a flat back cut; past the wood's `chop2.fellFraction` of the section cut it falls, toward the notch (the hinge steers), the stump keeping the notch's lower face and the trunk its upper face (`chop2.fellWedgeTrunk`: open).

durability.$comment: Tools wear (owner, 2026-11-11: the stone axe "should survive 32 hits of durability"; "stone pick wears too like axe, same with shovel": the stone pickaxe and the wooden shovel 32 each; owner, 2026-11-12: metal tools "have double durability": the metal axe, pickaxe and shovel 64 each): `items` gives a tool item its hits; a hit that counts (a chop, a bounce off a non-wood solid, or a break hit, with it held; at the swing's contact, never a miss, a swing through only leaves or a cancelled swing: owner, 2026-11-12, "Tools should only consume durability on hit.") uses one, and at none left the tool breaks (gone from its slot, `breakSound` played). A tool not listed never wears. `creativeWear`: whether tools wear where blocks are unlimited (false: creative's tools don't). The wear rides in the inventory record (dwell_protocol::inventory, a slot's `wear`).

breaking.$comment: Which tool breaks which blocks faster (owner, 2026-11-10: "pickaxe, shovel, and axe. Stone and Metal variants"): `classes` maps a tool class to the blocks (by name) it is the right tool for, each block in at most one; `tiers` is a tier's break speed (a multiple of the bare hand's, 1), as a number or `{ speed }` (a hit's bite is not a tier's: it is 0.5 × the block's volume ÷ its hits to break, docs/BLOCK_DAMAGE.md §10, so a faster tier's bites are bigger; owner, 2026-11-12: "Metal tools break double sized bigger chunks off and reach 50% broken faster, which is when the blocks break. Also have double durability.": metal speed 2 × stone's; the metal axe's `biteM` and `chop2.bite` 2 × the stone axe's); `tools` gives an item (shared/inventory) its class and tier. A break of a block holding the right class goes at its tier's speed, anything else at 1 (dwell_protocol::chopping::break_speed). A tool's `contactS` is when its swing's head meets the block, seconds after the click (the arms' `break` clip strikes at 0.26 s; WORK_QUEUE item 25: the hit, its marks, drops, sound and wear land then, the server applying it that long after the request arrives; none: 0, at once); the axe's contact is its `swing`'s (`windupS` and the arc's time to the hit). The axe's swing (`tools` above) lands on a wood with `damage` (the log) as a hit of the `axe` class, as a pickaxe's on stone (WORK_QUEUE item 51; owner, 2026-11-12: "Like the others, felling on top"; docs/BLOCK_DAMAGE.md §12): hits to break, marks, drops, and the break felling the trunk above; the cut model above is kept for older saves' cuts and the chopping prototype. A tool's `repeatOnHold` (owner, 2026-11-12: "I wanted you to be able to hold the key down for tools like the axe."; a chopping tool's in `tools`, a break tool's here, never both): holding the use button keeps swinging it until let go, each swing a full one hitting what is aimed at then (wear on a hit only); a break tool's `repeatS` the time between its swings (default 0.5, at least its `contactS`).
